thresholds.meaning: (relative, absolute): a change is flagged when it exceeds both

highlights.title: Verdict accuracy: 110 right / 1 misleading / 0 wrong runs (was 88 / 23 / 0).
highlights.detail: Gone: the 21 packet_loss false positives from hole punching (now 0 of 90 clean-link runs; the whole-phase counter still shows the artefact in 20 of them, the settled count in none) and the 2 relay_fallback_failed on the lossy link's working relay path. Left: 1 packet_loss_missed on the lossy link (0 of 115 packets lost in the window, sampling).

highlights.title: Lossy link (lab-netem-pr):
highlights.detail: healthy and exit 0 in 3/3 (was degraded/exit 5 in 2/3); relay_compare ok 3/3 (was 1/3) and 10/10 extra runs; packet_loss 2/3 as before (11/13 with the extra runs), the count settled in every run; concurrency throughput 0.6-1.4 Mbps in 3/3 (was none) and 8/10 extra; runs 58-70.5 s (was 61-69 s).

highlights.title: Same outcomes, no failures:
highlights.detail: final paths 51 direct / 42 relay / 0 failed, 0 connections lost, QUIC counters in 93/93, as in campaign 2. Lab RTT/throughput/bind/connect unchanged; real-world numbers move with the internet route clusters.

highlights.title: Run durations:
highlights.detail: +2.0 s on every peer run from the 12 s latency phase (e.g. 12.6 -> 14.6 s, 20.3 -> 22.3 s); the lossy link's runs did not get longer.

highlights.title: Regressions and new findings:
highlights.detail: No outcome, RTT or throughput regression. Flagged changes are noise or artefacts: the lossy upload median 18.8 -> 1.5 Mbps (per run 1.3 / 27.8 / 1.5, bimodal on that link in every campaign) and concurrency 262 -> 156 (rw-easy-to-open) / 156 -> 280 (rw-open-to-easy) Mbps, which is the 200 ms tick quantization of the concurrency phase (an old measurement bug, now documented). New bug found in the extra lossy runs: an upload finishing just before the 8 s limit failed with 'closed stream' (1 of 13), and concurrency sized from a lucky fast transfer still gave no number in 2 of 13.
